deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is the blue paper wrapper (front cover) of a manuscript bundle. It carries three archival annotations.

(1) A shelfmark in ink, upper left: 'Cod. Ms. Riemann 9'. This is the Göttingen Niedersächsische Staats- und Universitätsbibliothek signature for the Riemann Nachlass item 9.

(2) An older printed-border paper label, upper right, with the handwritten text 'Pariser Auf-gabe XXII 9.' ('Paris problem', with the old ordering number XXII 9). This identifies the contents as Riemann's work on the Paris Academy prize question on heat conduction. The resulting memoir is the 'Commentatio mathematica, qua respondere tentatur quaestioni ab Illma Academia Parisiensi propositae', submitted 1 July 1861. It deals with when a quadratic differential form can be transformed to a sum of squares in connection with the heat equation in anisotropic bodies, and it introduces what is now the Riemann curvature tensor. It was published posthumously in the Gesammelte Werke (1876).

(3) A faint red pencil note in the centre. It most plausibly reads '11 Bl.' (11 Blätter), a librarian's leaf count for the bundle.

There are no derivations to reconstruct. The page only shows that the following folios belong to the Paris prize ('Wärmeleitung') material.
